painted-turtle.role: A basking omnivore that grazes plants and hunts insects and small fish, and cleans up carrion. Young are mostly carnivorous, shifting toward plants with age.

chorus-frog.diet: Small insects and other tiny invertebrates
chorus-frog.fact: A chorus frog's comb-like call carries up to half a mile across the marsh.
chorus-frog.role: A tiny insectivore whose spring chorus fills the marsh. It eats small invertebrates and is itself vital prey for herons, mink, and snakes.

wetland-salamander.diet: Worms, insects, small invertebrates, and even small vertebrates
wetland-salamander.shelter: Damp burrows near fishless breeding pools
wetland-salamander.fact: Tiger salamanders are among the largest land salamanders in North America.
wetland-salamander.role: A voracious burrowing carnivore that hunts worms and invertebrates near breeding pools. Larvae grow in fishless water and can even turn cannibal.

dragonfly.diet: Flying insects as adults; aquatic larvae eat mosquito larvae and tadpoles
dragonfly.shelter: Emergent reed stems; larvae live in the water
dragonfly.fact: Dragonflies catch up to 95% of the prey they chase, among Earth's best hunters.
dragonfly.role: A top invertebrate predator both in the air and underwater. Adults hawk flying insects while aquatic nymphs devour mosquito larvae and tiny fish.

sources.name: Natural History Museum - Dragonflies: The ultimate hunters

damselfly.diet: Small flying insects as adults; larvae eat aquatic invertebrates
damselfly.shelter: Waterside vegetation; larvae among submerged plants
damselfly.fact: Damselflies fold their wings together over the back at rest, unlike dragonflies.
damselfly.role: A slender aerial insectivore that snatches midges and mosquitoes with its legs. Its aquatic nymphs hunt tiny invertebrates and feed marsh fish and frogs.

water-strider.diet: Insects and larvae trapped on the water surface; also scavenges
water-strider.shelter: Still water surfaces among emergent plants
water-strider.fact: Water striders ride the surface on legs coated in thousands of tiny hairs.
water-strider.role: A surface-skating predator and scavenger that seizes insects trapped in the water film. It is easy prey for fish, frogs, and wading birds.

freshwater-fish.diet: Algae, plankton, insect larvae, and small invertebrates
freshwater-fish.fact: Minnow schools are the foundation that herons, otters, and mink all depend on.
freshwater-fish.role: The forage base of the wetland food web. These schooling fish graze algae and plankton and eat insect larvae, then feed nearly every predator in the marsh.

american-bittern.diet: Fish, frogs, insects, crayfish, snakes, and small mammals
american-bittern.shelter: Platform nests hidden low in dense reeds
american-bittern.preferredHabitat: Tall marsh vegetation over shallow water
american-bittern.fact: The bittern freezes bill-skyward, swaying like a reed to vanish in the marsh.
american-bittern.role: A secretive ambush predator of the reed beds. It stands motionless, then seizes fish, frogs, and insects, relying on stripy camouflage to stay hidden.

sources.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds - American Bittern

belted-kingfisher.diet: Small fish and crayfish, plus other aquatic prey
belted-kingfisher.shelter: Tunnel burrows dug into earthen banks
belted-kingfisher.preferredHabitat: Clear water with perches over fishable shallows
belted-kingfisher.fact: Kingfishers dive headfirst into the water with their eyes closed to grab fish.
belted-kingfisher.role: A plunge-diving fish specialist that watches from a perch and dives on small fish and crayfish. It nests in tunnels dug metres into stream banks.

sources.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds - Belted Kingfisher

northern-leopard-frog.diet: Insects, spiders, worms, and other small animals
northern-leopard-frog.fact: Leopard frogs escape with erratic zig-zag leaps straight back into the water.
northern-leopard-frog.role: A wide-mouthed generalist that eats almost any small animal it can swallow, from insects to smaller frogs. It is key prey for herons, mink, and snakes.

sources.name: U.S. National Park Service - Northern Leopard Frog

snapping-turtle.diet: Fish, aquatic plants, carrion, and almost anything it can catch
snapping-turtle.preferredHabitat: Deep still water with a soft mud bottom
snapping-turtle.fact: Adult snapping turtles have almost no natural predators and can live for decades.
snapping-turtle.role: A heavily armored omnivore and scavenger lurking on the pond bottom. As an adult it sits near the top of the wetland food web, eating fish, ducklings, plants, and carrion.

marsh-wren.diet: Insects and spiders picked from marsh vegetation
marsh-wren.shelter: Woven dome nests among cattails and bulrushes
marsh-wren.fact: Males build many dummy nests and even destroy neighbours' eggs.
marsh-wren.role: A tiny, feisty insectivore of the reeds. It gleans insects and spiders from stems and famously builds several decoy nests to court a mate.

sources.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds - Marsh Wren

prothonotary-warbler.diet: Insects and spiders; some snails, fruit, and seeds off-season
prothonotary-warbler.shelter: Tree cavities and nest boxes over standing water
prothonotary-warbler.fact: It is one of only two North American warblers that nest in tree cavities.
prothonotary-warbler.role: A glowing-gold swamp warbler that gleans insects and spiders over the water. Unusually for a warbler, it nests in cavities, often above standing water.

sources.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds - Prothonotary Warbler

green-heron.diet: Mainly small fish; also insects, crustaceans, and frogs
green-heron.shelter: Stick nests in trees and shrubs overhanging water
green-heron.fact: The green heron drops bait on the water to lure fish within striking range.
green-heron.role: A small, crafty heron of shady shallows and one of few tool-using birds. It fishes patiently and sometimes baits the surface to draw fish close.

sources.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds - Green Heron

hooded-merganser.diet: Small fish, crayfish, aquatic insects, and amphibians
hooded-merganser.shelter: Tree cavities and nest boxes near water
hooded-merganser.fact: Hooded merganser ducklings can dive for their own food at just one day old.
hooded-merganser.role: A small diving duck with a serrated bill for gripping slippery prey. It pursues fish, crayfish, and insects underwater and nests in tree cavities.

sources.name: Cornell Lab All About Birds - Hooded Merganser

spotted-turtle.diet: Aquatic plants, insects, worms, mollusks, and small invertebrates
spotted-turtle.shelter: Basking logs and shallow, muddy-bottomed water
spotted-turtle.fact: Each spotted turtle wears a unique pattern of yellow polka dots on its shell.
spotted-turtle.role: A small, declining omnivore that forages underwater for plants and invertebrates. It basks on logs and buries in mud when startled.

sources.name: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service - Spotted Turtle

common-yellowthroat.diet: Insects and spiders gleaned from low vegetation
common-yellowthroat.shelter: Bulky grass cups low in cattails and sedges
common-yellowthroat.fact: The male's black bandit mask is a signal that rivals will attack on sight.
common-yellowthroat.role: A masked marsh warbler that gleans insects and spiders from dense low cover. It skulks through cattails and briars in search of prey.
